analysis.title: "Absolutely Zero Idea" Rerun: Goldman's Top Derivs Trader Dusts Off 2018 Playbook... And It Ends At S&P 6,294
key_insights: Goldman derivatives strategist Brian Garrett compared every major market's move since the S&P Oct 6 peak with its Sept 24 to Dec 24, 2018 move. Equities are close, especially tech, while credit has barely moved.

Through Thursday's close the Nasdaq 100 was down 15.1% from the peak, 69% of its 2018 drawdown of 21.8%. The S&P was down 8.2%, 42% of its 19.5% drop, and the Russell 2000 down 6.2%, 24% of its 25.7%.

Replaying the rest of the 2018 path from Thursday's close implies another 12% on the S&P to about 6,294, another 8% on the Nasdaq 100 and another 21% on the Russell. From around 7,020 after Friday's drop, 6,294 is roughly 10% away (author's napkin math).
The 2018 low came 65 trading days after the peak and Friday was day 33. On that clock the low is due in the first full week of January (author's math).
Credit is the largest difference from 2018. CDX IG is 5bps wider (15% of the 2018 move) and HY 38bps wider (28% of 136bps). A full replay implies roughly 27bps more in IG and 98bps in HY.

Rates have done about half the work. 10Y swaps are 23bps lower (64% of the 2018 rally), 5Y 17bps lower (42%), 2Y only 2bps (7%). The front end does not price a policy response, since the Fed is still hiking into a hot CPI and GS economists expect a third hike in March.
Havens failed. Gold is down 10.8% versus +5% in 2018 and the yen is 1% weaker versus +2.1% in 2018, printing -215% and -49% of the 2018 move.
Cross-asset overshoots and no-shows: copper is down 13.1%, more than twice its 2018 decline, crude is down 7% versus 41% in 2018, AUDUSD is at 160% of its 2018 move and USDMXN at 127%.

GS Panic Index is about 9 out of 10. Dealers are short gamma (about $1bn) and are modeled short vega. Thursday's S&P advance-decline spread of -426 was the worst of the year, and one-month implied vol on the average S&P stock is about 38, the 93rd percentile of the past decade.

The S&P implied move for the week was 1.9% and the index realized that full move in one session twice in four days. The implied move through next Friday is 3.00%. Spot VIX is about 6 vols above the front-month future, the most inverted since April 2025.
VIX at 30.3 is within 6 points of the Christmas Eve 2018 peak of 36.1 while the S&P is only about halfway through the 2018 drawdown. Fear is running ahead of price.

Desk color: clients are playing offense via equity vol by selling skew and fading wing bids on both sides, not buying calls. Clients faded the VIX spike with puts and put 1x2s, and in NVDA (down about 39% since early October) they lift call spreads and call spread collars while long-only supply hits cash.
GS desk trades: QQQ Dec 31 680/720 call spreads, XLP Jan 15 85/100 bearish risk reversals, and Feb 19 120% worst-of calls on NVDA/AVGO/INTC.
Across 2,258 GS baskets, first-half performance is inversely related to second half (slope -0.33, R² 0.40). Baskets that more than doubled in 1H have a median 2H return of about -50%.
Author view is bearish on rallies. A credit scare and Fed surrender made the 2018 low, and neither has occurred, so rallies are treated as rentals.

market_movers.rationale: NVDA is down about 39% since early October with long-only supply hitting the cash desk. Clients are lifting call spreads and call spread collars to keep some upside.

sector_views.rationale: Tech leads the drawdown, with the Nasdaq 100 at 69% of its 2018 drawdown and a global tech liquidation following the Anthropic IPO hangover.
Staples are being used as a hedge, but hedge funds are net selling them after the best run since the dot-com peak. Put-call skew is in the 3rd percentile over 20 years.

risk_factors: The 2018 path implies another 12% downside on the S&P to about 6,294 and 21% on the Russell.
Credit could be late and widen to catch up, with IG +27bps and HY +98bps in a full replay.
No Fed backstop while the Fed is hiking into a hot CPI.
Gold and the yen are failing as hedges.
Six down days plus a close below the 200DMA historically preceded drawdowns of 26%, 17% and 30%.

vol_and_positioning: GS Panic Index is about 9 out of 10 and dealers are short gamma by about $1bn and short vega in this range.
VIX is at 30.3 versus the 2018 peak of 36.1. Spot VIX is about 6 vols above the front-month future, the most inverted since April 2025.
S&P advance-decline spread of -426 was the worst of the year. One-month implied vol on the average S&P stock is about 38, the 93rd percentile of the past decade.
S&P implied move for the week was 1.9% and 3.00% through next Friday. The index realized the weekly move in a single session twice in four days.
Clients are selling skew and fading wing bids on both sides. One client bought the Dec 16 20/18 put spread 30K times as a 1x2.
Staples put-call skew is in the 3rd percentile of the past 20 years. GS Prime shows staples among the most net sold sectors this month.
QQQ RSI is near 33 and positioning is washed out.
geopolitical: Crude is down only 7% versus a 41% collapse in 2018, which the author attributes to Hormuz.
cross_bank_references: Both Barclays and Goldman's Rich Privorotsky were drawing the same 2018 parallel.
Barclays made the same point: the bigger problem for stocks is that nobody sees a Fed backstop.
Privorotsky said the market probably pivots when the central banks do.

tension_points.bull_case: Positioning is washed out, the Panic Index is at 9, clients are selling vol and QQQ is nearly oversold. All three prior 200DMA episodes began with a bounce.
tension_points.bear_case: The 2018 low needed a credit scare and a Fed surrender. IG has done 15% of its move, the front end 7%, and the Fed is still hiking.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A credit scare or Fed pivot would change the read on the low. Until then rallies are treated as rentals.

theme_stances.key_argument: Equities have done roughly half the 2018 job while credit and the front end have barely moved, so more downside remains.
theme_stances.evidence: assume the 2018 map still has plenty of road left on it

theme_stances.key_argument: Gold and the yen have moved the wrong way versus 2018, so they fail as hedges.
theme_stances.evidence: A hedge that falls 11% alongside the thing it was hedging is just another long.
